L_quote_based_comparison.reason: BLOCKED: no Databento key is stored in Strata's credential store, the environment or a .env file.
how: Open https://databento.com and choose Sign up to create an account.
Databento states that new users receive $125 of free credit, usable for historical data, shared by the whole team, applied before any charge and expiring six months after it is issued.
Sign in and open the API keys page of the portal (https://databento.com/portal/keys). A key is created with the account: a 32-character string that starts with db-.

Before the first download open the Billing page of the portal (https://databento.com/portal/billing). Databento's documentation says the remaining credit is shown there and that the account has a monthly usage limit you can set; it says further historical requests are blocked once the month's usage exceeds that limit. Set the limit to an amount you accept. Strata cannot see the credit or the limit: neither has an API.
In Strata open Settings, "Data provider keys", paste the key into the Databento field and press Save. The key goes to the operating system's credential store and is never shown again.

Run the check: Data -> Readiness -> "Check Databento" or `strata access databento` in a terminal. It makes free metadata requests only and ends with the exact price of a small sample, quoted by Databento itself.

To download that sample, run it again with a budget that covers the quoted price, for example `strata access databento --budget 1`. Nothing billable is requested without a budget, and never more than it.
L_quote_based_comparison.unverified: This adapter has never run against the live service: until it has, what it would retrieve is the provider's documentation, not a measurement.

M_question_typed_by_the_user.sentence: How often does SPY's first 9:30ET candle, predict its overall day?

read_as.hypothesis: The direction of the first candle of the session and the direction of the session agree more often than unrelated directions would.
read_as.method: On every SPY session with intraday bars: the direction of the first 5/15/30 minutes (close against the open) is compared with the direction of the whole session (open to close) and with the direction of the rest of it (the candle's close to the session's close). Up and down candles are counted separately, each against all sessions.
interpretation_notes: The length of the first candle was not stated, so 5-, 15- and 30-minute candles are all measured rather than one being assumed.

"The day" is measured twice. Open to close is the day as a whole, and the first candle is part of it: some agreement is built in. From the candle's close to the session's close is what was still unknown when the candle ended.
A candle's direction is its close against the session's open. Sessions whose candle closed exactly at the open have no direction and are left out; so are sessions without intraday bars.

variants: first 5 min up: session closes above its open
first 5 min down: session closes below its open
first 5 min up: close is above the 09:35 price
first 5 min down: close is below the 09:35 price
first 15 min up: session closes above its open
first 15 min down: session closes below its open
first 15 min up: close is above the 09:45 price
first 15 min down: close is below the 09:45 price
first 30 min up: session closes above its open
first 30 min down: session closes below its open
first 30 min up: close is above the 10:00 price
first 30 min down: close is below the 10:00 price
M_question_typed_by_the_user.verdict: The direction of SPY's first candle matched the direction of the whole session (open to close) on 58.0% to 64.8% of sessions, more the longer the candle, against about 50.0% if the two were unrelated. Most of that is the candle itself, which is part of the day it is compared with. From the end of the candle to the close it matched on 50.4% to 51.2%, against about 50.0% for unrelated directions: that is no more than chance produces, for every candle length measured.
findings: First 5 minutes: matched the whole session (open to close) on 58.0% of 2,714 sessions (95% interval 56.1% to 59.8%; 50.0% if unrelated); matched the rest of the session (09:35 to the close) on 50.7% of 2,714 sessions (95% interval 48.9% to 52.6%; 50.0% if unrelated).

First 15 minutes: matched the whole session (open to close) on 61.1% of 2,731 sessions (95% interval 59.3% to 63.0%; 50.0% if unrelated); matched the rest of the session (09:45 to the close) on 50.4% of 2,731 sessions (95% interval 48.5% to 52.3%; 50.0% if unrelated).

First 30 minutes: matched the whole session (open to close) on 64.8% of 2,728 sessions (95% interval 63.0% to 66.5%; 50.1% if unrelated); matched the rest of the session (10:00 to the close) on 51.2% of 2,728 sessions (95% interval 49.4% to 53.1%; 50.0% if unrelated).
limitations: Only sessions with intraday bars can be measured: 2,731 of them, 2016-01-04 to 2026-11-25.

A match with the whole session is not a forecast: the candle's own move is inside the open-to-close move it is compared with. Only the rest-of-session figures describe what was still unknown when the candle closed.
Direction only: a session that closes one cent above its open counts the same as one that closes 2% above it. Nothing here says how far the session went.
Probabilities describe the underlying's behaviour. They are not option returns and say nothing about trading costs.

decision.chosen: Run on the 142 qualifying sessions that are covered

said.text: Here is how I read that strategy. The entry rule fires on 143 sessions (2024-01-18 to 2026-11-23). 142 pass every check on stored option observations (142 on trade prints, with the contract stored, a print inside the entry window and the exit window covered): 99.3% of them. 1 has the contract stored but no trade inside the entry window. A run confirms each one: these are sessions the stored data supports, not trades. Not specified, so I assumed defaults you can edit: expiration, stop loss, exit rule.
read_as: Condition: previous session fell 0.5% or more (close-to-close)
Entry: 10:00 ET - you said "10:00 AM Eastern" - once per eligible session
End-of-day exit: 15:55 ET (before the 0DTE contracts expire) [assumed]
Costs: $0.65 commission per contract; quotes fill at the bid/ask; trade prints fill at the print with no extra slippage [assumed]

said.text: Only 142 of the 143 qualifying sessions in the period you asked for have usable trade prints. the contract is stored but did not trade inside the entry window: no print recent enough to fill at (1).
Running: Options backtest.

The entry rule fired on 143 sessions, but only 142 of them have usable observed option prices; the remaining 1 could not be tested and are not part of these figures. Historical options backtest on option trade prices, 2024-01-18 to 2026-11-23: 142 trades made a net profit of $3,052.40 after $184.60 in commissions (3.1% on starting capital). 45.1% of trades were winners; the average winner was $243.39 against an average loser of -$160.57, for $21.50 per trade and a profit factor of 1.24. The largest winner was $3,829.70 and the largest loser -$458.30; the deepest drawdown was -2.4% of equity. The per-trade profit has a t-statistic of 0.66, which is below the conventional threshold of two, so the edge is not statistically distinguishable from zero in this sample.

experiment.sentence: Compare entry times from 9:30 to 11:00 in 15-minute increments, prior-day declines from 0.5% to 3%, 0DTE versus 1DTE, and several profit targets.

said.text: Running 252 configurations of one strategy on stored option trade observations. Varied: entry time (New York): 09:30, 09:45, 10:00, 10:15, 10:30, 10:45, 11:00; days to expiration: 0DTE, 1DTE; profit target, % of premium: 25%, 50%, 100% (assumed); previous-day decline, %: 0.5%, 1%, 1.5%, 2%, 2.5%, 3% (assumed). "several profit targets" names none: 25%, 50% and 100% of the premium are assumed. No step was given for the decline: 0.5% is assumed. No time zone was stated: the entry times are read as Eastern time and shown in New York time. Every configuration counts as a trial; the result is read as a map of how the outcome depends on the settings, not as a search for the best cell.

dims.text: entry times from 9:30 to 11:00 in 15-minute increments

said.text: 252 of 252 configurations traded. 213 of them (84.5%) end above zero; the median result is +1,020.80. The best, 09:45, 1DTE, 50%, 0.5%, made +8,927.05 over 143 trades (t +2.81; as the best of 252 configurations that is p = 1.00 after adjusting for the search, 0.005 before). Chosen on the earlier sessions alone, the best would have been 10:45, 1DTE, 100%, 1.5% (+287.30 a trade over 27 trades before 2026-01-20); on the later sessions it made -130.12 a trade over 14. Across the 126 configurations with enough trades in both parts, the ranking by the earlier part and by the later part correlate at -0.56: the ranking tends to REVERSE: what looked better earlier mostly looked worse later. Coverage ranges from 99.3% to 100% of the signals: configurations are not all tested on the same sessions. Both parts are history that has now been examined; neither is evidence of an edge.
